expectation: x8 located behaves like X7's decider; x8 hidden holds many more pairs but stays in bound; control hidden fails on false merges
known_risks: the far-duplicate recheck labels follow LGA and distance closely; distance is also a feature, so the located view can reward a reviewer's own heuristic
the hidden view removes coordinates only; a list without LGA is not tested
uniqueness uses name cores after removing a fixed type-word list; names whose distinguishing word is on that list (e.g. 'Comprehensive' vs 'Basic') collapse to one core
the uniqueness index counts registry duplicates as other facilities, which makes a duplicated name look common
150 pairs: with about 60-90 different pairs, one false merge can put the Wilson upper bound over 5%
question: With name uniqueness within the LGA as evidence, and trained to know when location is missing, does the decider keep errors and false merges in bound in a held-out state (Anambra), with location and without it?

arms.augmented: control features, trained on every labelled pair twice: as labelled and with both points removed (distance 0, coordinates-missing 1), each copy in its pair's fold; separate thresholds for located (out-of-fold on originals) and hidden pairs (out-of-fold on copies)
arms.control: X7's ungated decider: [cross-encoder logit, log1p km, LGA agree via aliases, coordinates missing]; no location-free copies; its located thresholds are used for hidden pairs too (today's behaviour)
arms.reference: match-everything, scored under the same rule; it must fail
arms.x8: augmented plus log1p(n) and core_equal * [n == 0] * same_lga, where n = other facilities (GRID3 and HFR together, by id) in the GRID3 record's state and LGA whose name core equals the GRID3 name's core; core = folded name minus TYPE_WORDS; empty core counts as n = 99; the GRID3 record, its own HFR twin and the pair's HFR record are excluded

rule.cross_encoder: X0's recipe with Edo, Kano, Ondo, Lagos, FCT, Oyo and Anambra held out; weights pinned below
rule.development: 1,707 labelled pairs: X7's development labels (with the X4 corrections and the Oyo restore), the X7 Lagos pack as exported, then the far-duplicate recheck outcomes (corrections.json) over the 37 pairs it rechecked
rule.error_bound: errors among auto-decided <= 3% and Wilson 95% upper bound <= 10%
rule.false_merge_bound: different pairs auto-matched / all different pairs <= 2% and Wilson 95% upper bound <= 5%
rule.informative: void unless the test holds at least 60 different pairs
rule.population: the X8 pack (data/review_packs/nigeria_facilities_anambra_x8_2026-11-23, 150 Anambra pairs: 70 review_band, 40 lookalike, 40 near_miss) marked same_entity or different; read once, after this file
secondary: control_hidden_pass (expected to fail: the missing-coordinates defect)
results by pair kind and on the review band
development out-of-fold false merges per arm and view
rule.uniqueness_helps_hidden: on every seed, x8 hidden settles more pairs than augmented hidden and auto-matches no more different pairs

views.hidden: the same pairs and labels with both points removed (distance 0, coordinates-missing 1)

rule.x8_pass: informative; every seed of x8 located meets fewer_held, error_bound and false_merge_bound; and every seed of x8 hidden meets hidden_ok

test.blind: the reviewer sees neither the engine's decision nor the pair's kind; the hidden view needs no second review
test.construction: data/scripts/build_x8_pack.py (build_x4_pack.py with STATE = 'Anambra', BAND 70, STRESS 40): 70 of the engine's 279 Anambra review pairs (one per GRID3 facility, salted-hash order), 40 lookalike and 40 near_miss

why: The far-duplicate recheck showed the reviewer judging by 'the same name in the same LGA is one facility unless the name marks another'; 1.6% of GRID3 and 1.7% of HFR records share an exact name with another in their LGA. It also showed a defect: with coordinates removed, X7's decider auto-matched 20 of the 37 rechecked pairs, 9 of them different, because a missing point is scored as 0 km and the missing flag's weight is 0.0
